name: perf_reg_validate
prose: Validates a perf register mask. It returns -EINVAL if mask is 0 or if mask has any bit set outside the low PERF_REG_RISCV_MAX bits (REG_RESERVED is ~((1ULL << PERF_REG_RISCV_MAX) - 1)); otherwise it returns 0. It reads only its argument and has no side effects.
note: Contract removed (depends on the macro value of PERF_REG_RISCV_MAX, not stated numerically here). Code checked at perf_regs.c:19-27. Slice cut head; mechanical-only rejections.

name: riscv_hartid_to_cpuid
prose: Returns the logical CPU id whose entry in cpuid_to_hartid_map equals hartid. It scans i from 0 to NR_CPUS - 1 and returns the first i for which cpuid_to_hartid_map(i) == hartid; if no entry matches it returns -ENOENT. It reads the map without taking a lock and has no side effects.
note: Contract removed. No substantive reviewer disagreement (reviewer 15 said formal contract weaker than prose); code checked at smp.c:71-80. Slice cut head.

name: handle_scalar_misaligned_load
prose: Emulates a misaligned scalar or FP load at regs->epc for the faulting address regs->badaddr. It always begins by recording a PERF_COUNT_SW_ALIGNMENT_FAULTS software event and setting this CPU's misaligned_access_speed to RISCV_HWPROBE_MISALIGNED_SCALAR_EMULATED. It then returns -1 (regs->epc unchanged) if unaligned_enabled is false, if the trap came from user mode and current->thread.align_ctl has PR_UNALIGN_SIGBUS, or if get_insn fails. After that it sets regs->epc = 0 and decodes the instruction (LW, LD and LWU on 64-bit, FLD, FLW, LH, LHU and the compressed C.LD, C.LDSP, C.LW, C.LWSP, C.FLD, C.FLDSP, C.LHU, C.LH, plus C.FLW and C.FLWSP on 32-bit); an unrecognised instruction restores regs->epc = epc and returns -1. If the instruction is a floating-point load and CONFIG_FPU is not enabled it returns -EOPNOTSUPP with regs->epc still 0. It then copies len bytes from addr with copy_from_user (user mode) or memcpy (kernel mode); if copy_from_user fails it returns -1 with regs->epc still 0. On success it writes the loaded value (sign-extended for the signed forms) into the destination integer or FP register and sets regs->epc = epc + INSN_LEN(insn), where insn may have been rewritten for the compressed forms, and returns 0.
note: Reviewer 15 (omits -EOPNOTSUPP with regs->epc left 0 when !CONFIG_FPU) RIGHT: traps_misaligned.c:241,304-305. Old prose also said epc is restored on failures; it is not restored after the copy_from_user failure (line 308-309) or the -EOPNOTSUPP return. Slice cut head; real function at 220-331.

name: riscv_v_vstate_ctrl_set_current
prose: Implements the PR_RISCV_V_SET_CONTROL prctl for the current task. It returns -EINVAL if neither has_vector() nor has_xtheadvector() is true, or if arg has any bit outside PR_RISCV_V_VSTATE_CTRL_MASK (0x1f). It takes cur from the low two bits of arg: OFF (1) returns -EPERM if the current task's cur setting is not already OFF; ON (2) is accepted; DEFAULT (0) replaces cur with the task's current cur value; any other value (3) returns -EINVAL. It then takes next from bits 2-3 and the inherit flag from bit 4; if next is DEFAULT, OFF or ON it calls riscv_v_ctrl_set(current, cur, next, inherit) and returns 0; otherwise (next == 3) it returns -EINVAL without having called riscv_v_ctrl_set.
note: Reviewer 15 and earlier ones concern the old contract (removed; function reads current). Prose rechecked against vector.c:261-300 and macro values in prctl.h:321-327; -1 is -EPERM. Slice cut head.

name: kvm_pmu_get_fixed_pmc_index
prose: Maps an SBI PMU event index to the fixed counter index. It extracts etype with kvm_pmu_get_perf_event_type(eidx) (the type field, bits 16-19 under SBI_PMU_EVENT_IDX_TYPE_MASK) and ecode as eidx & 0xFFFF. If etype is not SBI_PMU_EVENT_TYPE_HW it returns -EINVAL. If ecode is SBI_PMU_HW_CPU_CYCLES (1) it returns 0; if ecode is SBI_PMU_HW_INSTRUCTIONS (2) it returns 2; any other code returns -EINVAL. It has no side effects.
note: Reviewer 15 (type is masked to bits 16-19, not 16-31) RIGHT (sbi.h:248-249). Old prose said codes 0 and 1; the code compares against SBI_PMU_HW_CPU_CYCLES = 1 and SBI_PMU_HW_INSTRUCTIONS = 2 (sbi.h:183-184). Contract removed. Code at vcpu_pmu.c:150-164. Slice cut head.

name: kvm_riscv_vcpu_pmu_ctr_stop
prose: Handles the SBI PMU counter-stop call for ctr_mask counters starting at ctr_base. It has one return, which always returns 0 after storing sbiret in retdata->err_val (0 if no error was recorded). sbiret is sticky: once set it is overwritten only by later errors, and it also gates the snapshot copy. It sets sbiret = SBI_ERR_INVALID_PARAM and jumps to out if kvm_pmu_validate_counter_mask fails, and SBI_ERR_NO_SHMEM and jumps to out if SBI_PMU_STOP_FLAG_TAKE_SNAPSHOT is set but kvpmu->snapshot_addr is INVALID_GPA. Then, for each set bit i of ctr_mask, it computes pmc_index = array_index_nospec(i + ctr_base, RISCV_KVM_MAX_COUNTERS) and skips counters not set in pmc_in_use. For a firmware counter: an event code >= SBI_PMU_FW_MAX sets SBI_ERR_INVALID_PARAM and jumps to out (ending the loop); a counter not started sets SBI_ERR_ALREADY_STOPPED and goes on; otherwise it marks the firmware event stopped and copies its value to pmc->counter_val. For a counter with a perf_event: if started it adds perf_event_pause(...) to counter_val and clears started, else sets SBI_ERR_ALREADY_STOPPED; with SBI_PMU_STOP_FLAG_RESET it then releases the perf event. A counter with neither sets SBI_ERR_INVALID_PARAM (the loop continues). If the snapshot flag is set and sbiret is still 0 it copies the overflow bit (if set in pmc_overflown) and counter_val into kvpmu->sdata and marks the snapshot dirty. With SBI_PMU_STOP_FLAG_RESET it sets event_idx to SBI_PMU_EVENT_IDX_INVALID, clears the in_use and overflown bits and, when the snapshot flag is set, clears the counter's bit in sdata->ctr_overflow_mask and marks the snapshot dirty; this reset step is done whether or not sbiret holds an error. After the loop, if the snapshot is dirty and kvm_vcpu_write_guest of the snapshot fails, sbiret becomes SBI_ERR_FAILURE.
note: Reviewer 1 (already-stopped/invalid counters not stopped; snapshot only when shmem_needs_update) right: vcpu_pmu.c:662-678,714-717. Reviewer 15 (overflow mask cleared under RESET even if an error was recorded) RIGHT: 699-711 is unconditional on sbiret, unlike the copy at 687. Slice cut head; real function at 627-723.

name: set_mm
prose: Static inline helper with two variants. In the MMU build (context.c:207-225) it first sets cpu in mm_cpumask(next). Then, if the use_asid_allocator static key is enabled, it calls set_mm_asid(next, cpu); otherwise it clears cpu in mm_cpumask(prev) and calls set_mm_noasid(next). Because the clear happens after the set, when prev == next on the no-ASID path cpu ends up cleared in that mask, not set. In the !MMU variant (context.c:277-281) the body is empty and nothing happens.
note: Reviewers 1-3 (prev == next noasid branch clears the bit set just before) all RIGHT: context.c:218,222. Slice listed only the first variant; both are described. Contract empty.

name: parse_boot_command_line
prose: Parses the s390 boot kernel command line. It sets __kaslr_enabled to IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_RANDOMIZE_BASE), copies early_command_line into command_line_buf with strscpy (truncating if too long), and loops over the copy with next_arg(). For each parameter name it applies the following checks independently (separate if statements): mem with a value sets memory_limit to memparse(val) rounded down to PAGE_SIZE; vmalloc with a value sets vmalloc_size (rounded up to _SEGMENT_SIZE) and vmalloc_size_set; dfltcc with a value of off, on, def_only, inf_only or always sets zlib_dfltcc_support to the matching constant (other values leave it); facilities with a value calls modify_fac_list; debug-alternative calls alt_debug_setup(val), even if val is NULL; nokaslr clears __kaslr_enabled; cmma runs kstrtobool(val, &enabled) and sets cmma_flag = 0 only when it parses and enabled is false; under CONFIG_KVM prot_virt sets prot_virt_host = 1 only when kstrtobool succeeds and gives true; relocate_lowcore sets MFEATURE_LOWCORE only if test_facility(193); earlyprintk sets boot_earlyprintk; debug sets boot_console_loglevel to CONSOLE_LOGLEVEL_DEBUG; bootdebug sets bootdebug and copies val into bootdebug_filter if present; quiet sets CONSOLE_LOGLEVEL_QUIET; ignore_loglevel sets boot_ignore_loglevel; loglevel sets boot_console_loglevel = simple_strtoull(val, NULL, 10) without checking val for NULL, then raises it to CONSOLE_LOGLEVEL_MIN if it is lower. Unrecognised parameters are skipped. The function returns void.
note: Reviewer 15 (loglevel without a value calls simple_strtoull(NULL); cmma=on/prot_virt=off not applied) RIGHT: ipl_parm.c:289-300,317-321. Slice cut head; real function at 246-323.

name: __physmem_alloc_range
prose: Finds a free physical address range of size bytes. It computes nranges as from_ranges if nonzero, else physmem_info.range_count (the code does not check that from_ranges <= range_count), raises align to at least 8, and starts with pos = max. In a loop over nranges, from the last range downward, it reads the range with __get_physmem_range(nranges - 1, ...) and lowers pos to the range end if that is smaller; if round_up(min, align) + size > pos it leaves the loop; otherwise it takes addr = round_down(pos - size, align); if addr is below the range start it moves to the next lower range (nranges--); if [addr, addr + size) intersects a reserved area (__physmem_alloc_intersects) it sets pos to the start of that intersection and retries; otherwise it stores nranges in *ranges_left when ranges_left is non-NULL and returns addr. If the loop ends without a result it calls die_oom(size, align, min, max) when die_on_oom is true and returns 0 otherwise (die_oom is a separate boot-time error reporter). The function only searches: it does not record the allocation itself; the callers physmem_alloc_range and physmem_alloc do.
note: Reviewer 1 (code requires from_ranges <= range_count) right as an implicit precondition, now stated. Prose rechecked against physmem_info.c:272-306. Slice cut head.

name: physmem_alloc_range
prose: Allocates a physical range of size bytes for the reserved-range type type. It lowers max to min(max, physmem_alloc_pos), calls __physmem_alloc_range(size, align, min, max, 0, NULL, die_on_oom), and if the result is nonzero records it with _physmem_reserve(type, addr, size). It always emits a boot_debug line with the address (also when addr is 0) and returns addr, which is 0 when no range was found and die_on_oom did not stop the boot.
note: Prose rechecked at physmem_info.c:308-319; no reviewer feedback (fixed-unreviewed). Slice cut head.

name: physmem_alloc
prose: Allocates size bytes top-down below physmem_alloc_pos for reserved-range type type. It calls __physmem_alloc_range(size, align, 0, physmem_alloc_pos, physmem_alloc_ranges, &ranges_left, die_on_oom) and returns 0 if that returns 0 (state unchanged). If the type's existing range does not end directly below the new block (range->start != addr + size): when range->end is already nonzero it allocates a struct reserved_range (with die_on_oom true) below physmem_alloc_pos, then calls __physmem_alloc_range again for the data below that address with the remaining ranges (returning 0 if that fails, without updating the globals), copies the old *range into the new structure and chains it as range->chain; in both sub-cases it then sets range->end = addr + size. For types other than RR_VMEM it emits a boot_debug line. It then sets range->start = addr, physmem_alloc_pos = addr and physmem_alloc_ranges = ranges_left and returns addr.
note: Prose rechecked at physmem_info.c:321-359; no reviewer feedback. Notable: on the failed second allocation in the split branch the earlier reserved_range allocation is not undone. Slice cut head.

name: physmem_alloc_or_die
prose: Thin wrapper: it returns physmem_alloc(type, size, align, true), i.e. a top-down allocation with die_on_oom set; it adds no logic of its own.
note: Prose rechecked at physmem_info.c:361-365. Slice cut head.

name: setup_kernel_memory_layout
prose: Computes the s390 kernel virtual memory layout in the decompressor and returns the address space limit asce_limit; it has a single return at the end. It first overwrites vmemmap_size from ident_map_size (pages = ident_map_size / PAGE_SIZE, section-aligned, times sizeof(struct page)), so a previous value of vmemmap_size is not used. It estimates the virtual memory size with get_vmem_size and chooses asce_limit = _REGION1_SIZE (4-level) when CONFIG_KASAN is on, when __NO_KASLR_END_KERNEL > _REGION2_SIZE, or when the estimated size exceeds _REGION2_SIZE and kaslr_enabled(); otherwise asce_limit = _REGION2_SIZE (3-level). It sets rte_size to _REGION2_SIZE only in the case __NO_KASLR_END_KERNEL > _REGION2_SIZE and to _REGION3_SIZE otherwise, adjusts vmax with adjust_to_uv_max(asce_limit) (and under KASAN to at most KASAN_SHADOW_START) and clamps vsize. It chooses kernel_start: a random THREAD_SIZE-aligned slot below vmax when kaslr_enabled() (position 0 if get_random fails), a constrained position below vmax when vmax < __NO_KASLR_END_KERNEL or vsize > __NO_KASLR_END_KERNEL, else __NO_KASLR_START_KERNEL. It then writes the globals __kaslr_offset, MODULES_END, MODULES_VADDR, VMALLOC_END, VMALLOC_START, vmalloc_size (reduced to fit, and under KMSAN to a third), __memcpy_real_area, __abs_lowcore, vmemmap, vmemmap_size, ident_map_size (reduced so the identity map does not overlap vmemmap), max_mappable and, under CONFIG_RANDOMIZE_IDENTITY_BASE, __identity_base, and prints boot_debug lines. It takes no locks and returns asce_limit.
note: Reviewer 15 (precondition wrongly requires vmemmap_size initialised; code overwrites it first) RIGHT: startup.c:330. Reviewers 1-2 (contract omits asce limit/max_mappable) addressed. Slice cut head; real function at 318-445.

name: startup_kernel
prose: Entry point of the s390 decompressor; it takes no arguments, returns void and ends by calling jump_to_kernel(&psw) (that function is defined elsewhere and was not read). In order: setup_lpp, store_ipl_parmblock, uv_query_info, setup_boot_command_line and parse_boot_command_line; it computes nokaslr_text_lma (mem_safe_offset aligned to _SEGMENT_SIZE) and safe_addr, reserves RR_DECOMPRESSOR from 0 to safe_addr, reserves RR_INITRD when CONFIG_BLK_DEV_INITRD is set and parmarea.initrd_size is nonzero, and copies parmarea.oldmem_base and oldmem_size into oldmem_data (the old-memory area is recorded in oldmem_data, not reserved with physmem_reserve). It then runs read_ipl_report, SCLP and facility/machine detection, cmma_init, sanitize_prot_virt_host, detect_max_physmem_end, setup_ident_map_size, setup_vmalloc_size, setup_kernel_memory_layout (giving asce_limit), physmem_set_usable_limit, detect_physmem_online_ranges, save_ipl_cert_comp_list and rescue_initrd. It picks text_lma: a random location from randomize_within_range when kaslr_enabled(), falling back to nokaslr_text_lma when 0, ORed with the low offset bits of __kaslr_offset; sets __kaslr_offset_phys = text_lma - TEXT_OFFSET, calls kaslr_adjust_vmlinux_info, reserves RR_VMLINUX and calls deploy_kernel((void *)text_lma), then re-reserves RR_DECOMPRESSOR only up to _decompressor_end, picks amode31_lma (random below 2 GB when KASLR is on, else text_lma - amode31_size) and reserves RR_AMODE31. It then runs clear_bss_section, kaslr_adjust_relocs, kaslr_adjust_got, setup_vmem, dump_physmem_reserved, copy_bootdata and __apply_alternatives(ALT_CTX_EARLY), stores __kaslr_offset_phys | 1 (or 0) in lowcore->vmcore_info, builds a PSW with address __kaslr_offset + vmlinux.entry and mask PSW_KERNEL_BITS, and calls jump_to_kernel(&psw).
note: Reviewer 15 (oldmem region not reserved via physmem_reserve; only oldmem_data set) RIGHT: startup.c:521-522, now stated. Slice cut head; real function at 489-639. Details of the called helpers are not described.

name: ecb_paes_do_one_request
prose: Crypto-engine callback that runs one ECB protected-key AES request whose skcipher walk was already prepared. It calls ecb_paes_do_crypt(ctx, req_ctx, true). If that returns -EKEYEXPIRED it calls cond_resched() and returns -ENOSPC so the engine reschedules the request; in that case it does not zero req_ctx->param, does not decrement ctx->via_engine_ctr and does not finalize the request. For any other nonzero rc it calls skcipher_walk_done(walk, rc). In every case other than -EKEYEXPIRED it then zeroes req_ctx->param with memzero_explicit, decrements ctx->via_engine_ctr and calls crypto_finalize_skcipher_request(engine, req, rc) with bottom halves disabled around those two calls, and returns 0 (the result travels through the finalization).
note: Reviewer (on -EKEYEXPIRED returns -ENOSPC before zeroing param and without finalizing) RIGHT: paes_s390.c:544-554, prose already said so. Prose rechecked at 532-566. Slice cut head.

name: cbc_paes_setkey
prose: Sets the key for a CBC protected-key AES transform. It calls paes_ctx_setkey(ctx, in_key, key_len) and, if that returns nonzero, returns that code; then paes_convert_key(ctx) and returns its code on failure (on both early failures ctx->fc is not written). Then it selects fc from ctx->pk.type: CPACF_KMC_PAES_128, _192 or _256 for the AES-128, AES-192 and AES-256 protected key types, and 0 for any other type. It then writes ctx->fc = fc when fc is nonzero and cpacf_test_func(&kmc_functions, fc) is true, and 0 otherwise. It returns 0 if fc is nonzero (including when cpacf_test_func fails, in which case ctx->fc is 0 but the return is still 0), and -EINVAL if the key type gave fc == 0.
note: Reviewer 1 (returns 0 even if cpacf_test_func fails; early errors do not clear ctx->fc) RIGHT: paes_s390.c:639-641 (rc depends on fc, not on ctx->fc) and 616-622. Slice cut head; real function at 607-646.

name: cbc_paes_do_crypt
prose: Runs the CBC protected-key AES operation over the prepared walk. If req_ctx->param_init_done is false it reads ctx->pk_state under ctx->pk_lock: PK_STATE_NO_KEY gives rc = -ENOKEY, PK_STATE_CONVERT_IN_PROGRESS gives -EKEYEXPIRED, PK_STATE_VALID copies the protected key into param->key and sets param_init_done, and any other state gives the state value if negative or -EIO. A nonzero rc is returned at once without touching the walk. Otherwise it copies walk->iv into param->iv and loops while walk->nbytes != 0: it processes the full-block part n with cpacf_kmc(ctx->fc | req_ctx->modifier, ...); if k > 0 bytes were processed it copies param->iv back into walk->iv and sets rc = skcipher_walk_done(walk, nbytes - k) (so rc is whatever that call returns). If k < n and maysleep is false it returns -EKEYEXPIRED (walk left mapped); if maysleep is true it calls paes_convert_key, returns its error if nonzero, and otherwise refreshes param->key under ctx->pk_lock and continues the loop. When the loop ends the function returns the last rc (0 initially, then the last skcipher_walk_done result).
note: Reviewer (can return -EIO or paes_convert_key errors, not only -ENOKEY/-EKEYEXPIRED) RIGHT, now stated (paes_s390.c:672-674,699-703). Also the final rc is the last skcipher_walk_done result (692-695). Slice cut head; real function at 648-714.

name: cbc_paes_crypt
prose: Starts a CBC protected-key AES request with the given modifier. It calls skcipher_walk_virt(walk, req, false); on failure it jumps to out, returning that error with req_ctx->param zeroed and skcipher_walk_done not called. Otherwise it stores modifier and sets param_init_done to false. If ctx->via_engine_ctr is zero it tries cbc_paes_do_crypt(ctx, req_ctx, false) synchronously and returns 0 (param zeroed) if that returns 0. If rc is still 0 (the synchronous attempt was skipped because the engine counter was nonzero) or is -EKEYEXPIRED, it increments ctx->via_engine_ctr and calls crypto_transfer_skcipher_request_to_engine; if that returns anything other than -EINPROGRESS it decrements the counter again. If the resulting rc is not -EINPROGRESS (a transfer failure, or any other error from the synchronous attempt) it calls skcipher_walk_done(walk, rc). At out, if rc is not -EINPROGRESS it zeroes req_ctx->param with memzero_explicit; it returns rc. On -EINPROGRESS the param is left in place for the engine.
note: Reviewer (walk_virt failure returns -errno without skcipher_walk_done) RIGHT, stated (paes_s390.c:731-733,757-763). Slice cut head; real function at 716-765.

name: __diag288
prose: Static inline wrapper around the diagnose 0x288 instruction. It packs func and timeout into register pair r1 (even and odd halves) and action and len into register pair r3, sets rc to -EINVAL, and executes diag r1,r3,0x288 inside an asm volatile with "cc" and "memory" clobbers. If the diagnose completes without a program exception, the following lhi sets rc to 0 and it returns 0. If the diag instruction raises an exception covered by the EX_TABLE entry, the lhi is skipped and rc keeps the initial -EINVAL, which is returned. The function does not itself validate func, timeout, action or len.
